clue.text: Offspring of Chesterton's man, one destined to succeed?

indicators.note: offspring of someone puts the parent's name first, so the man's name comes before the child

parts.note: G. K. Chesterton wrote the novel The Man Who Was Thursday; the possessive gives the S
offspring means a child

explanation.surface: A question about the son of some character from Chesterton, tipped for a bright future.
explanation.walkthrough: The old rhyme says 'Thursday's child has far to go', so such a child is fated to go far, the question mark marking the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme the child born on that weekday has far to go, idiomatically meaning will do well in life.

clue.text: Unconvincing report from Selkirk, perhaps?

explanation.definitionFit: A tall story told by someone back from distant places is the proverbial example of a report nobody quite believes.

clue.text: Inclination to remove one of three basics from education
